L2t: Gough Island, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, hosts millions of seabirds that are preyed upon by introduced house mice.
L3t: The mouse eradication on Gough Island was planned as an aerial baiting operation conducted in the austral winter, and the first bait drop was delayed until the 2020 attempt was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
L4t: The mouse eradication program on Gough Island began in 2021, when the first aerial bait drops were made.
L2f: Gough Island is a British-owned island whose mice were introduced only in the last few decades by a modern scientific research station.
L3f: The Gough Island mouse eradication was launched in the early 2010s after a rapid feasibility study, with the first baiting carried out soon after that study ended.
L4f: The mouse eradication program on Gough Island first began in 2011.
